thread:
lee: FYI we accidentally pulled ~12h of auth/edge logs for vuln triage yesterday. Too broad. Need hard limits on exports + clearer unwrap rules for KMS.
maria: Which exporter? snapshot or streaming?
lee: snapshot-exporter-prod. It generated a signed S3 URL with 6h TTL. That should never happen for triage.
devops: Proposal: enforce policy at exporter that caps triage snapshots to 30m by default, require explicit scope export:forensics to go beyond, and mint STS-style ephemeral tokens for KMS unwrap with max ttl 10m. Signed URLs rotate every 5m.
auditor-bot: DLP detected peripheral identifiers in that export. Ticket SEC-501 opened.
security-bot: Logged export metadata and linked SEC-501.
maria: Add an OPA policy gate and require request include audit:ticket_id. If missing, deny. We'll also require decrypt logs to emit requestor, ticket, and token id to CloudTrail.
oncall: I'll implement URL revocation and add a runbook step to rotate presigned URLs to 5m and immediately revoke on suspicious DLP flags. Opening TICKET-ENG-760.
devops: Add a pre-export DLP scan webhook; if risk_score > 0.5 auto-pause and create a manual review task. Streaming exports get 1h max and must pass scrub for PII.
lee: OK. Owners: devops updates exporter + DLP hook, maria authors OPA policy, oncall runbook + rotation ticket, compliance to sign off on KMS key policy change. I'll capture outcomes in SEC-501.
maria: Also suggest telemetry: metric for "exports_over_default_ttl" to alert if policy bypassed.
lee: Good. Thanks all. Will sync if compliance needs clarifications.
